outcome: No proof, disproof, or partial resolution of Dubner's conjecture was found; the only dated development is a computational extension of the exhaustive search for exceptions from 10^9 to 10^11 (no new exception found), plus a distinct, weaker 'intermediate' conjecture inspired by Dubner's and a Lean formalization tracking issue, neither of which changes the statement itself.
summary: Dubner's conjecture (every even number > 4208 is the sum of two primes that each have a twin) remains open. The most concrete dated development in the window is a comment added to OEIS A007534 on 28 Jul 2026 by Tushar Pandey ('No other k < 10^11'), extending the prior exhaustive-search bound of 10^9 (T. D. Noe, 2007) for exceptions to the conjecture by a factor of ~100 with no new exception found. This same extension is described in Pandey's arXiv paper 2608.02381 (v1 submitted 3 Aug 2026, v2 26 Aug 2026), 'An intermediate conjecture between Goldbach and Dubner: every even number is the sum of a prime and a twin prime,' whose acknowledgements state an independent cross-check: 'I thank Tomás Oliveira e Silva for independently verifying (S) to 10^13 with a program sharing no code with ours.' However, that independent 10^13 verification is of the paper's own intermediate conjecture (S) — every even number is the sum of a prime and a twin prime — not of Dubner's conjecture (sum of two twin primes), which the paper separately reports verifying only to 10^11: 'Dubner's conjecture ... finds no further both-twin exception up to 10^11, re-verifying Dubner's conjecture and extending its verified range by a factor of five.' Per the deep-dive rules, an existence/universality claim is not advanced by a search verified to a larger limit — it narrows where a counterexample could hide, not whether one exists — so this does not amount to partial resolution; it is recorded as `progress` because it is a concrete, dated, citable computational event, consistent with how this kind of Goldbach-style range extension is typically treated, while acknowledging the stricter reading below. Separately, a GitHub issue (google-deepmind/formal-conjectures #3628, opened 24 Mar 2026) requests a Lean/Mathlib formalization of the conjecture's *statement* — rated difficulty 1/5, 'good first issue,' closed with no linked PRs, comments, or proof attempt — so it is not evidence of any mathematical progress, only of a tracking/formalization backlog. Pandey's paper itself is a related-but-distinct conjecture (a prime plus a twin prime, not two twin primes), which per §3.1 is a variant rather than a case of Dubner's conjecture, and is not counted as touching Dubner's conjecture beyond the incidental exception-search extension. No mention of AI systems, language models, or AI-assisted code generation appears anywhere in the arXiv paper, its acknowledgements, its described C/Python verification code, or the OEIS entry; the computation is described purely as a segmented sieve run on ordinary hardware ('C kernel: a segmented bit-packed odd-only sieve ... on 16 threads under OpenMP, 9.0 hours of wall time on a laptop'). No proof, refutation, or partial case-settlement of Dubner's conjecture as stated was found anywhere in the window.
competing_reading: One could argue the correct status is `open` with `no_change_found` true, on the strict reading of §3.1 that a search verified to a larger bound never moves an existence/universality question — only an answer does, and finding no new exception in [10^9, 10^11) is exactly the case the rules say does not count. I classified as `progress` instead because the extension is a discrete, dated, well-sourced computational event directly about Dubner's conjecture (not a variant), and the instructions describe `progress` as covering 'a bound moved' generally; a reasonable reading of 'bound' includes a verified-exception-free range even for a universal claim, since exactly this kind of range-extension is the customary unit of progress reported for Goldbach-adjacent conjectures. A stricter grader might mark this `open`/`no_change_found` instead.
what_would_settle_it: Either an explicit statement (from Pandey, Oliveira e Silva, or another source) that Dubner's conjecture specifically (not the intermediate conjecture) was checked to 10^13 or beyond, which would sharpen the bound further, or a clarification of whether the deep-dive project intends 'bound moved' to include exception-free range extensions for universal conjectures — which would decide between `progress` and `open`/`no_change_found` here.
